questions.stem: Project TIGER was launched in India in:
questions.explanation: Project Tiger launched on 1 April 1973 at Jim Corbett National Park. Started with 9 tiger reserves; now 55+ reserves. National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA) is the statutory oversight body (established 2005).
questions.subject: Environment

questions.explanation: Established 1936 as Hailey National Park (after Governor Malcolm Hailey), renamed to Jim Corbett National Park in 1957 in honour of the British-Indian hunter-turned-conservationist. Located in Nainital district, Uttarakhand. originally Hailey National Park.
questions.subject: Environment

questions.stem: Match the national park with its CHIEF fauna. A. Kaziranga. B. Gir. C. Sundarbans. D. Keoladeo (Ghana). List-II: 1. Royal Bengal Tiger (mangrove habitat). 2. Migratory birds. 3. One-horned rhinoceros. 4. Asiatic lion.
questions.explanation: Kaziranga (Assam) — one-horned rhino stronghold (population ~2,600). Gir (Gujarat) — ONLY home of Asiatic lion outside Africa. Sundarbans (WB) — Royal Bengal Tigers adapted to mangrove ecosystem. Keoladeo / Bharatpur (Rajasthan) — UNESCO site famous for migratory birds (notably Siberian cranes historically).
questions.subject: Environment

questions.stem: Consider the following about India's BIODIVERSITY HOTSPOTS. India has how many of the global 36 biodiversity hotspots entirely or partly within its borders?
questions.explanation: India shares 4 biodiversity hotspots: (1) Himalaya, (2) Indo-Burma, (3) Western Ghats + Sri Lanka, (4) Sundaland (Nicobar Islands). Each has >1,500 endemic vascular plant species and has lost >70% of primary vegetation — Myers et al's definition.
questions.subject: Environment

questions.stem: Consider the following about INDIA'S TIGER POPULATION per the 2022 All-India Tiger Estimation. 1. Total tiger population is around 3,167 (minimum estimate). 2. Madhya Pradesh has the highest number of tigers among Indian states. 3. Corbett Tiger Reserve has the highest individual reserve tiger population. 4. Ranthambore Tiger Reserve is in Madhya Pradesh. Which are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement 4 is WRONG — Ranthambore is in RAJASTHAN (Sawai Madhopur district). 2022 estimation: ~3,167 tigers (~3,682 as per updated July 2023 figure). MP leads in state tiger count (~785). Corbett leads in reserve tiger count (~260).
questions.subject: Environment

questions.stem: The CHIPKO MOVEMENT of the 1970s is associated with:
questions.explanation: Chipko (literally 'to stick / hug') — non-violent movement in Uttarakhand (then UP), women of Reni village led by Gaura Devi in 1974 hugged trees to prevent contractor logging. Sundarlal Bahuguna + Chandi Prasad Bhatt were other leaders. Inspired global forest-conservation activism. hugging trees to prevent logging.

questions.stem: India's FIRST Biosphere Reserve, notified in 1986 and covering parts of Tamil Nadu, Karnataka and Kerala, is the:
questions.explanation: The Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve was India's first, notified on 1 September 1986 under the UNESCO MAB programme. It spans roughly 5,500 km² across Tamil Nadu, Karnataka and Kerala, encompassing Bandipur, Mudumalai, Nagarhole and Wayanad sanctuaries. Nanda Devi came next in 1988; Sundarbans and Manas were both designated in 1989.

questions.stem: The Asiatic lion (Panthera leo persica), India's only wild lion population, is presently found only in and around which national park?
questions.explanation: Asiatic lions survive in the wild only in the Gir landscape of Saurashtra, Gujarat — Gir National Park and adjoining sanctuaries. The 2020 census recorded around 674 lions. Translocation to Kuno (Madhya Pradesh) was directed by the Supreme Court in 2013 but is pending; Kuno was repurposed in 2022 for Project Cheetah.

questions.stem: On the IUCN Red List, which of the following categories indicates the highest extinction risk for a species that still survives in the wild?
questions.explanation: IUCN extinction-risk categories, from lowest to highest threat: Least Concern → Near Threatened → Vulnerable → Endangered → Critically Endangered → Extinct in the Wild → Extinct. CR therefore designates the highest risk for a species still extant in the wild. Examples for India: Great Indian Bustard, Gharial, Pygmy Hog (all CR).

questions.stem: Project Elephant, the centrally-sponsored conservation scheme covering elephant ranges, corridors and the Gajatame initiative, was launched by the Government of India in:
questions.explanation: Project Elephant was launched in February 1992 by the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, twenty years after Project Tiger (1973). India has 33 notified Elephant Reserves. The decoy distractors map to other landmark years: 1972 (Wildlife Protection Act), 1986 (Environment Protection Act), 2002 (Biological Diversity Act).

questions.stem: The MAB (Man and the Biosphere) Programme under which biosphere reserves are designated worldwide is run by which UN agency?
questions.explanation: The Man and the Biosphere (MAB) Programme is a UNESCO initiative started in 1971 to balance conservation with sustainable use. Biosphere reserves on the World Network are designated by UNESCO — India has 12 such reserves, of which 12 are nationally notified and a subset (Nilgiri, Nanda Devi, Sundarbans, Gulf of Mannar, etc.) appear on the UNESCO WNBR list.

questions.stem: Under the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972, as amended by the 2022 Amendment that rationalised the schedules, species enjoying the HIGHEST level of legal protection are now listed in:
questions.explanation: The Wild Life (Protection) Amendment Act, 2022 collapsed the original six schedules into four: Schedule I — highest protection (e.g., tiger, elephant, leopard, gharial, gangetic dolphin); Schedule II — lesser-protected animals; Schedule III — plants; Schedule IV — CITES-listed scheduled specimens. The earlier Schedule V (vermin) was abolished. Pre-2022, hard recall asked about Schedules I+II combined.

questions.stem: Project Hangul, a species-specific conservation initiative active since 1970 in Dachigam National Park, targets the recovery of which endangered animal?
questions.explanation: The Hangul or Kashmir stag (Cervus hanglu hanglu, formerly C. elaphus hanglu) is the only Asiatic survivor of the red deer family and the state animal of Jammu & Kashmir. Project Hangul began in 1970 at Dachigam (around Srinagar) after the population had crashed below 200. The 2019 census put the count near 237, still classified Critically Endangered on the IUCN Red List.
